title: Draw Things CLI Qwen Image 2512 Book Cover Recommendation Rules

target_runtime.output_shell_note: Use --output "$HOME/Dev/tmp/file.png" or an unquoted ~/path. Tilde does not expand inside single quotes.
target_runtime.scope: Text-to-image book-cover artwork with embedded title, series name, and publisher name.

do_not_assume: That SDXL LoRAs are compatible with Qwen Image 2512; treat them as SDXL-only unless the installed CLI explicitly confirms compatibility.
That numeric sampler ID 0 means Euler in every CLI build; confirm the mapping against the installed build or a controlled test.
That upscaler selection alone improves text legibility or corrects misspelled text.
That model-generated cover text is production-ready without OCR and human proofing.

sampler.note: The user's command example uses sampler 0. Keep this as a configurable candidate, not a universally verified Euler mapping. Validate against the installed draw-things-cli version.
sampler.validation: Run the same seed/prompt/settings with sampler IDs exposed by the installed build; compare visual quality, repeatability, and runtime.

steps.note: Qwen Image 2512 reference workflows commonly use 50 steps and CFG 4; test lower steps for draft throughput.

cfg.note: Begin around CFG 4. Raise modestly only if prompt adherence is weak; reduce if colours, edges, or composition become harsh.

resolution.note: Use dimensions supported by the installed model/runtime. Prefer aspect ratio matching the intended cover; upscale only after composition is approved.

upscaling.policy: Select by image structure, not genre name alone. Compare at least two allowed upscalers on a representative crop.
upscaling.print_note: A 4x upscale increases pixel dimensions, not the amount of verified detail. Inspect fine lines, faces, and all text after upscaling.

embedded_text.policy: Prompt each text string exactly, with its placement and hierarchy. Keep title short where possible. Use quotes in the prompt if they help the model distinguish literal text.
embedded_text.fallback: If exact text is not reliably rendered, generate a clean text-safe cover composition and typeset text separately in a layout tool.

watch_out_for: may soften thin line art or fine texture
inspect for invented texture and oversharpening
can create halos or harsh edges; avoid as default for delicate watercolor
not the default for photorealistic or textured painterly images
check faces, foliage, and tiny text
may not reach target print dimensions alone

profiles.goal: Prioritise exact embedded title, series, and publisher lettering over visual complexity.
profiles.prompt: Professional portrait book cover. Simple elegant background with one clear focal illustration and generous uncluttered typography area. Render these exact strings verbatim and in this hierarchy: title "[TITLE EXACTLY]"; series name "[SERIES EXACTLY]"; publisher name "[PUBLISHER EXACTLY]". Preserve spelling, capitalization, spacing and word order. Title largest, series smaller, publisher smallest but legible. High contrast, balanced margins, no other words or labels.
profiles.negative_prompt: misspelled text, changed capitalization, missing words, duplicated letters, extra words, pseudo-text, random symbols, watermark, logo, cropped letters, overlapping text, low contrast, text over faces, decorative clutter.
profiles.why: Simplifying the artwork reduces competing demands on text rendering; use separate typesetting if exact copy is mandatory.
constraints: replace all bracket placeholders before generation
do not trust generated text without proofing

actions: recommend separate typesetting if exact text fails
enforce white background and black closed contours
inspect eyes, line edges, and halos
preserve paper grain and pigment blooms
check geometry, texture, halos and facial detail
generate one image per run during baseline testing
increase dimensions only after measuring memory and latency

positive_prompt_order: exact title, series name, publisher name
negative_prompt_strategy: List failure modes relevant to the chosen profile, not a giant universal list.
For text-heavy covers: misspellings, extra words, pseudo-text, watermark, cropped or overlapping letters.
For coloring art: color, gray fill, gradients, shadows, broken contours, scratchy lines, filled black blobs.
For children: frightening expressions, gore, adult themes, clutter, tiny detail.
For photorealism: CGI sheen, impossible geometry, oversaturated HDR, unnatural reflections, halos.
Avoid contradictory negative terms that suppress desired style; for example do not ban texture in a pencil sketch.
prompt_strategy.iteration_policy: Fix one class of error per iteration: composition first, then text zone, then typography, then details/upscale. Keep seed fixed for comparisons if the CLI supports a seed argument.

hard_fail_conditions: title, series, or publisher name misspelled when exact embedded text is required
unsafe or age-inappropriate content for the specified audience
important text cropped or outside safe margins
coloring-book line art has pervasive gray shading or open contours
upscaler introduces visible halos, face damage, or destructive line merging

confidence_policy.high: Documented runtime compatibility and repeatable evaluation on local build.
confidence_policy.medium: Reasonable profile prior but needs local image comparison.
confidence_policy.low: Model/upscaler interaction or style match is uncertain; benchmark before automation.

validation_plan: Record draw-things-cli version and confirm model loads successfully.
Confirm sampler numeric IDs for the installed build; do not assume IDs are stable across versions.
Generate a fixed-seed baseline at 1024x1536, 40 steps, CFG 4, sampler ID 0.
For each profile, compare one setting at a time: steps 32/40/50; CFG 3.5/4.0/4.5; two candidate upscalers.
Inspect full image and 160-pixel thumbnail; inspect 100% crops for line quality, faces, text and artifacts.
Run OCR plus manual proofreading on title, series and publisher strings.
Test final dimensions and bleed/safe-area rules in the actual print layout.
Store run metadata, seed, prompt, negative prompt, CLI version, model hash, settings, output checksum and evaluation score.
